senses.definitionCN: 为服务支付额外的钱
senses.example: Passengers tipped the porter a pound.
senses.exampleCN: 乘客给了搬运工一镑小费。
senses.why: The noun of money becomes the act of giving it.
senses.whyCN: 钱的名词变成给钱的行为。

senses.title: The top of a structure or region
senses.definition: the highest or furthest point of something, such as a mountain
senses.definitionCN: 某物最高或最远之点，如山顶
senses.example: Snow covered the tip of the mountain.
senses.exampleCN: 山顶覆盖着雪。
senses.why: The farthest end upward is still an end.
senses.whyCN: 向上的最远端仍是末端。

senses.title: To tip off: warn in advance
senses.definition: to warn someone privately before something happens
senses.definitionCN: 事前私下提醒或告发
senses.example: Someone tipped off the police about the raid.
senses.exampleCN: 有人向警方事先透露了突袭计划。
senses.why: Information tilts the outcome before the event lands.
senses.whyCN: 消息让结局在事件落地前先行倾斜。

intro.en: Tip is a Germanic word of double origin: one line from Old Norse or Low German meaning the point or end, another from later usage meaning to tap or strike, which led to tilting and to the slang of small payment.
intro.cn: tip 在日耳曼语中有双线来源：一线出自古诺斯语或低地德语，意为尖端；另一线为后期用法「轻敲、击打」，引申出倾斜与小费的俚语义。

items.en: Tip meant the point or top of a thing.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 tip 指物体的尖端或顶部。

items.en: Tip named ends of blades, fingers and poles.
items.cn: 中古英语 tip 用来指刀刃、指尖与杆的末端。

items.en: The verb grew: to tip meant to tap, then to tilt and overturn.
items.cn: 十六世纪动词扩展：由轻敲而倾斜、翻倒。

items.en: Tipping grew into handing over, and slang made a tip a small gift of money.
items.cn: 十七世纪 tipping 衍生为递出，俚语中 tip 成为小额赏钱。

items.en: A tip as a hint spread from racing slang into everyday advice.
items.cn: 十九世纪 tip 表内幕消息，由赛马俚语进入日常建议。

items.en: Modern usage keeps ends, tilts, fees and hints side by side.
items.cn: 现代用法并置尖端、倾斜、小费与提示。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alike short -ip words; the second sorts end-and-hint neighbours.
note.cn: 第一组是 -ip 结尾的形近短词；第二组列出末端与提示义的近邻。

entries.definition: a light knock, or a device controlling water flow
the highest part of something
to put something briefly into liquid
the pointed top of a mountain or the highest level
a formal word for money given for service
a slight or indirect suggestion

normalIntro.en: Real links: the tip of the iceberg, tip over, leave a tip, and a racing tip.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：冰山一角、翻倒、留小费，以及赛马内幕消息。

normal.en: A tip is the point your finger finds first.
normal.cn: tip 是手指最先碰到的那个点。

normal.en: The tip of the iceberg hides the mass below.
normal.cn: 冰山一角之下藏着整座冰山。

normal.en: Tip over shows the end swinging down.
normal.cn: tip over 是末端向下摆动的翻倒。

normal.en: A tip for the waiter is money at the end of the meal.
normal.cn: 给侍者的小费是餐尾递出的钱。

normal.en: A good tip tilts the game your way.
normal.cn: 一条好提示让局面朝你倾斜。

abstract.en: Every tip is where a thing runs out of itself.
abstract.cn: 每个 tip 都是事物耗尽自身之处。

abstract.en: A small lean, a small sum, a small hint: the word loves the small end of things.
abstract.cn: 一点倾斜、一笔小钱、一条小提示：这个词偏爱事物的细小末端。

abstract.en: Information is a weight; a tip is where it lands.
abstract.cn: 信息是重量，tip 是它落下的那一点。

examples.en: Only the tip of his boot showed under the snow.
examples.cn: 雪下只露出他的靴尖。

examples.en: She tipped her chair back while reading.
examples.cn: 她读书时把椅子往后翘。

examples.en: A friend tipped me off about the cheap flights.
examples.cn: 朋友提前告诉了我廉价航班的消息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踢破」——脚尖一踢踢破了罐子，罐子一斜倒出小费 → tip 尖端；倾斜；小费

root: 双线词干：一为古诺斯语/低地德语 tip「尖端、末端」；二为近代英语动词 tip「轻敲」，由此引申倾斜、倒出与赏钱。两线在发展中交汇。

sensesIntro.en: Tip marks the end of a thing, the tilt of a thing, and the small extra that changes either.
sensesIntro.cn: tip 标记事物的末端、事物的倾斜，以及改变两者的那份小小额外。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an extreme end that can lean, spill, or carry a small extra.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个能倾斜、能倾泻、也能承载小小额外的极端末端。

branches.en: Ends of blades, fingers and mountains.
branches.cn: 刀刃、指尖与山峰的末端。

branches.en: Tilting and emptying.
The small fee and the act of giving it.
The hint that shifts plans.
Advance warning that tilts outcomes.

intro.en: Tip is a short native stem; its items show compounds of ends, tilts and hints.
intro.cn: tip 是简短的本土词干；条目展示尖端、倾斜与提示的复合词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognates; tip is fully Germanic in origin.
latinIntro.cn: 无拉丁同源词；tip 完全源于日耳曼语。

items.meaning: the moment when change becomes unstoppable
items.example: The lake reached its tipping point.

items.meaning: a lorry whose back tilts to unload
items.example: A tipper delivered the gravel.

items.meaning: slightly drunk, unsteady on the feet
items.example: He sounded a little tipsy on the phone.
Keep the engine in tip-top shape.
The police acted on a tip-off.
items.exampleCN: 警方根据密报采取行动。

items.example: She touched the glass with a fingertip.

items.meaning: the end of the toe; to walk on it silently
items.example: He tiptoed past the sleeping dog.

items.meaning: a publication of hints, especially for betting or stocks
items.example: Racers studied the tip sheet.

definition_zh: 使疲劳；厌烦；轮胎
definition_en: to make someone feel they need rest, to lose patience, or (US spelling tire) a rubber ring round a wheel
core_image: 被拉松的橡皮筋；一圈包住车轮的橡胶
scene: 爬了一下午山，孩子们脚步慢下来。The long climb began to tire the children.
sceneCN: 这里 tire 是「使疲劳」（第 1 个义项：让体力耗尽）；句意：长时间的攀登开始让孩子们疲惫。

pos.zh: 轮胎（美式拼写，英式作 tyre）

derivatives.zh: tire 加 -ed，义为「疲倦的；厌倦的」
tire 加 -some，义为「烦人的；令人厌倦的」
tire 加 -ing，义为「累人的」

senses.title: To make someone need rest
senses.definition: to reduce someone's strength so that they want to rest
senses.definitionCN: 耗减体力使人想休息
senses.example: The long speech tired the audience.
senses.exampleCN: 冗长的演讲让听众疲倦。
senses.why: The core image is a strap stretched until it slackens.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是绷带被拉伸到松弛。

senses.title: To lose patience or interest
senses.definition: to become bored or unwilling to continue with something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事感到厌倦，不愿继续
senses.example: She never tires of explaining it.
senses.exampleCN: 她解释这事从不厌倦。
senses.why: Mental wear follows the same path as bodily wear.
senses.whyCN: 精神的磨损与身体的磨损同路。

senses.title: To become physically worn
senses.definition: to grow weak and slow through effort
senses.definitionCN: 因用力而渐感无力迟缓
senses.example: The horses tired before the last hill.
senses.exampleCN: 马匹在最后一座山前疲惫下来。
senses.why: The stretched thing finally slackens on its own.
senses.whyCN: 被拉伸之物最终自行松弛。

senses.title: A rubber ring round a wheel
senses.definition: a thick rubber ring fitted round the rim of a wheel (US spelling; British tyre)
senses.definitionCN: 套在轮辋上的厚橡胶圈（美式拼写，英式作 tyre）
senses.example: A nail went through the front tire.
senses.exampleCN: 一颗钉子扎穿了前轮胎。
senses.why: The wheel's outer band wears like a tired body and takes the word for wear.
senses.whyCN: 车轮外圈如同疲惫的身体会磨损，故借「磨损」之词。

senses.title: To exhaust completely
senses.definition: to tire someone fully, with no strength left
senses.definitionCN: 使人力气全无
senses.example: The march tired out the new soldiers.
senses.exampleCN: 行军把新兵累垮了。
senses.why: The stretching is carried to its full extent.
senses.whyCN: 拉伸被进行到极限。

senses.title: Tired of people and things
senses.definition: weariness directed at persons, tasks or repeated things
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、任务或重复之事生出的倦意
senses.example: He grew tired of the same questions.
senses.exampleCN: 他厌倦了同样的问题。
senses.why: Repeated strain wears a groove of dislike.
senses.whyCN: 反复的紧绷磨出一道厌恶的槽。

senses.title: Tired of the wheel: the spare
senses.definition: compound uses of the wheel sense, such as spare tire or tire pressure
senses.definitionCN: 轮胎义的复合用法，如备胎、胎压
senses.example: Check the tire pressure before the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前检查胎压。
senses.why: The rubber ring generates its own small family of phrases.
senses.whyCN: 橡胶圈生发出自己的一小族短语。

senses.title: Attire: the older dressing sense
senses.definition: in older English, dress or clothing, as in attire, built on this stem
senses.definitionCN: 旧英语中指装束，如 attire，建于此词干
senses.example: The knights wore rich attire.
senses.exampleCN: 骑士们衣着华贵。
senses.why: The old meaning survives mainly inside attire.
senses.whyCN: 旧义主要存活在 attire 之内。

intro.en: The verb tire comes from Old English tyrian, to wear out, related to the idea of drawing and stretching until slack. The wheel tire is a shortened form of attire, the band that dresses the wheel.
intro.cn: 动词 tire 出自古英语 tyrian「使耗损」，与「拉拽、拉伸至松弛」的观念相关；车轮义 tire 则是 attire（为车轮「着装」的轮箍）的缩略。

items.en: Tyrian meant to fail or wear out through strain.
items.cn: 古英语 tyrian 意为因拉拽而耗损。

items.en: Tiren covered both bodily wear and boredom.
items.cn: 中古英语 tiren 兼指身体疲劳与厌倦。

items.en: Atirer meant to arrange or dress, giving attire.
items.cn: 古法语 atirer 意为整理、穿着，生出 attire。

items.en: Tire appeared as the band that dressed a wheel, first of iron.
items.cn: 十五世纪 tire 指给车轮着装的轮箍，先是铁制的。

items.en: Rubber tires replaced iron bands on carriages and cars.
items.cn: 十九世纪橡胶轮胎取代车用铁箍。

items.en: British spelling settled on tyre, American on tire; the verb keeps both meanings.
items.cn: 英式拼作 tyre，美式拼作 tire；动词双义并存。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alike -ire words; the second sorts wear-and-wheel neighbours.
note.cn: 第一组是 -ire 结尾的形近词；第二组列出磨损与车轮义的近邻。

entries.definition: to pay for the use or work of something or someone
burning flames, or to dismiss from a job
the British spelling of the wheel band
to drain all the strength from someone
extreme tiredness, or to make someone so
the round frame the tire fits on

normalIntro.en: Real links: tired of waiting, tire out, spare tire, and never tire of.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：等得不耐烦、累垮、备胎，以及从不厌倦。

normal.en: Tire is the strap pulled until it slackens.
normal.cn: tire 是被拉到松弛的绷带。

normal.en: Boredom is wear of the mind, so it borrows the same word.
normal.cn: 厌倦是精神的磨损，所以共用这个词。

normal.en: A tire dresses the wheel as attire dresses you.
normal.cn: tire 给车轮着装，正如 attire 给你着装。

normal.en: Tire out pulls the stretching to the very end.
normal.cn: tire out 把拉伸进行到底。

normal.en: Never tire of it means the strap never slackens.
normal.cn: never tire of 意为绷带从不松弛。

abstract.en: Every tire is a story of something stretched and spent.
abstract.cn: 每个 tire 都是被拉伸、被耗尽的故事。

abstract.en: The wheel wears the road; the body wears the day.
abstract.cn: 车轮磨着路，身体磨着一天。

abstract.en: To rest is to let the strap draw back.
abstract.cn: 休息就是让绷带回缩。

examples.en: Reading in bad light tires the eyes.
examples.cn: 在昏暗光线下阅读使眼睛疲劳。

examples.en: He changed the flat tire by the roadside.
examples.cn: 他在路边换掉了瘪胎。

examples.en: The children tire quickly on hot afternoons.
examples.cn: 孩子们在炎热的午后很快疲倦。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太哑」——累得说不出话，声音都「太哑」了 → tire 使疲劳；轮胎

root: 双线词干：一为古英语 tyrian「使耗损、拉拽至疲」（动词疲劳义）；二为古法语 atirer「整理、穿着」，经 attire 缩略为车轮外箍的 tire。两源拼写重合。

sensesIntro.en: One tire spends strength and patience; the other wraps a wheel in rubber.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个 tire 耗去体力与耐心；另一个给车轮裹上橡胶。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something stretched until it slackens, or a band that hugs a wheel.
core.cn: 核心意象：被拉伸至松弛之物，或紧箍车轮的胶带。

branches.en: Bodily wear, caused and felt.
Wear of patience and liking.
The rubber ring and its phrases.
Stretching carried to the limit.
The old dressing sense inside attire.
branches.cn: 存活于 attire 的旧「着装」义。

intro.en: Tire takes plain English suffixes; its items show the wear family and wheel compounds.
intro.cn: tire 接朴素的英语后缀；条目展示磨损词族与车轮复合词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognates; tire is Germanic for the verb, French for the wheel band.
latinIntro.cn: 动词义无拉丁同源词，属日耳曼语；车轮义源自法语。

items.example: He was too tired to argue.
It was a long, tiring day.

items.meaning: annoying because it tires or bores
items.example: The paperwork was tiresome.
She is a tireless worker.
items.exampleCN: 她是个不知疲倦的劳动者。

items.example: The guests wore formal attire.

items.meaning: to withdraw from work or a room
items.example: He retired at sixty.

items.meaning: an extra wheel band kept for emergencies
items.example: The spare tire is under the boot floor.
items.exampleCN: 备胎在行李箱地板下面。

items.example: Her tireless effort saved the project.
items.exampleCN: 她不懈的努力挽救了项目。

definition_zh: 标题；头衔；所有权；冠军
definition_en: the name of a book or film, a name of rank, legal ownership, or a championship
core_image: 印在作品门口的名字；一枚挂在名下的法律标签
scene: 封面上烫金的书名在灯下闪光。She read the title of the novel aloud.
sceneCN: 这里 title 是「标题」（第 1 个义项：作品的名称）；句意：她大声读出那本小说的书名。

derivatives.zh: sub- + title，义为「副标题；字幕」
en- + title，义为「使有权；给……题名」
entitle 加 -ment，义为「应得的权利；津贴」

senses.title: The name of a work
senses.definition: the name given to a book, film, painting or piece of music
senses.definitionCN: 书籍、电影、画作或乐曲的名称
senses.example: The title of the film is three words long.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的片名有三个词。
senses.why: The core image is a name posted at the door of a work.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是挂在作品门口的名字。

senses.title: A name of rank or office
senses.definition: a word such as Doctor or Professor used before a name to show rank
senses.definitionCN: 置于姓名前表示身份的称呼，如 Doctor、Professor
senses.example: How should I address you — what title do you use?
senses.exampleCN: 我该怎么称呼您——您用什么头衔？
senses.why: The name on the door becomes the label on the person.
senses.whyCN: 门上的名字变成人身上的标签。

senses.title: Legal ownership
senses.definition: the legal right to own property, especially land or a car
senses.definitionCN: 拥有财产（尤指土地、车辆）的法定权利
senses.example: The title to the farm is held in trust.
senses.exampleCN: 农场产权由信托持有。
senses.why: Ownership is written as a label fixed to the thing owned.
senses.whyCN: 所有权被写成固定在物上的标签。

senses.title: A championship
senses.definition: the position of winning a competition, defended in later contests
senses.definitionCN: 竞赛夺魁的地位，可在后续赛事中卫冕
senses.example: She defends her title next month.
senses.exampleCN: 她下个月卫冕冠军。
senses.why: Championship is a label of rank held and guarded.
senses.whyCN: 冠军是一枚被持有和守护的等级标签。

senses.title: To give a name to a work
senses.definition: to give a title to a book, film or section
senses.definitionCN: 为书籍、影片或章节定名
senses.example: The chapter is titled Broken Glass.
senses.exampleCN: 该章题为「碎玻璃」。
senses.why: The posted name becomes an act of posting.
senses.whyCN: 门上的名字变成「挂名」这个动作。

senses.title: A written work as a catalogue item
senses.definition: a book or publication counted as one item in a list or library
senses.definitionCN: 在清单或图书馆中被计为一条的书籍或出版物
senses.example: The press issues twenty new titles a year.
senses.exampleCN: 该出版社每年推出二十个新书品种。
senses.why: A work is counted by its name-tag on the shelf.
senses.whyCN: 一部作品按书架上的名字标签被清点。

senses.title: A claim based on right
senses.definition: a ground or basis of right, as in the old phrase by the title of law
senses.definitionCN: 权利的依据，如旧语 by the title of law
senses.example: Their claim has no title in law.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的主张在法律上没有依据。
senses.why: The legal label extends to any ground of right.
senses.whyCN: 法律标签扩展为一切权利的依据。

senses.title: Titles in cards and church offices
senses.definition: in law and church use, the office or church from which a cleric takes his designation
senses.definitionCN: 法律与教会用语中，圣职人员所系的职位或教堂名义
senses.example: The priest held his title from an old abbey.
senses.exampleCN: 这位神父的职衔系于一座古老修道院。
senses.why: Rank labels branch into institutional forms.
senses.whyCN: 等级标签延伸出制度化的形态。

intro.en: Title comes from Old French title and Latin titulus, an inscription or label placed over something, which grew into names of works, ranks and ownership.
intro.cn: title 经古法语来自拉丁语 titulus「铭文、标签」，置于某物之上的标记，发展出作品名、头衔与产权诸义。

items.en: Titulus meant an inscription, a plaque or label fixed above a thing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 titulus 指铭文，固定于物上的牌子或标签。

items.en: Title kept the senses of inscription and chapter heading.
items.cn: 古法语 title 保留铭文与章节标题之义。

items.en: Title named book headings and legal grounds of right.
items.cn: 中古英语 title 兼指书名与法律权利依据。

items.en: Title spread to ranks and forms of address.
items.cn: 十五世纪 title 扩展至头衔与称谓。

items.en: The verb to title appeared with printed books.
items.cn: 随着印刷书籍出现，动词 title 产生。

items.en: Modern usage spans works, rank, property and championships.
items.cn: 现代用法涵盖作品、头衔、产权与冠军。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alike -itle words; the second sorts name-and-right neighbours.
note.cn: 第一组是 -itle 形近词；第二组列出名称与权利义的近邻。

entries.definition: small in size; spelled close but a different word
entries.definitionCN: 小的；拼写相近而非同词

entries.definition: a tiny mark or dot in writing
entries.definitionCN: 书写中的小点；微小的记号

entries.definition: a secondary title or printed translation of dialogue
words written at the top of a page or section
a signed legal document proving ownership
a position in a scale of status or authority

normalIntro.en: Real links: the title of a book, a job title, title deed, and winning the title.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：书名、职位名称、地契，以及夺冠。

normal.en: A title is the label fixed above the door of a work.
normal.cn: title 是挂在作品门楣上的标签。

normal.en: A job title pins the same label to a person.
normal.cn: 职位名称把同样的标签钉在人身上。

normal.en: A title deed is ownership written as a label.
normal.cn: 地契就是写成标签的所有权。

normal.en: Winning the title is holding the champion's label.
normal.cn: 夺冠就是握住冠军的标签。

normal.en: Entitle hands someone the right the label carries.
normal.cn: entitle 把标签所载的权利交到某人手中。

abstract.en: Every title is a short inscription that opens a claim.
abstract.cn: 每个 title 都是开启一项主张的简短铭文。

abstract.en: Names name things; titles give them standing.
abstract.cn: 名字称呼事物，title 给它们名分。

abstract.en: To hold a title is to keep the plaque polished.
abstract.cn: 持有头衔，就是把那块牌子时时擦亮。

examples.en: The title page lists the publisher and the year.
examples.cn: 扉页列出出版社与年份。

examples.en: He held the boxing title for three years.
examples.cn: 他保持了三年拳击冠军头衔。

examples.en: The house is titled in her name.
examples.cn: 这栋房子的产权登记在她名下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抬头」——抬头上写的正是标题与头衔 → title 标题；头衔

root: 单一词干：拉丁语 titulus「铭文、标签」，经古法语 title 进入英语。核心是「置于其上的标记」，由物名而人名，由名分而产权。

sensesIntro.en: Title begins as an inscription and grows into names, ranks, ownership and championships.
sensesIntro.cn: title 始于一块铭牌，长成书名、头衔、产权与冠军。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a label fixed above a thing, marking name, rank or right.
core.cn: 核心意象：置于其上的标签，标记者名称、等级或权利。

branches.en: Names of works, given and counted.
branches.cn: 作品之名，被赋予与被清点。

branches.en: Rank labels and institutional offices.
Ownership and grounds of right.
The champion's guarded label.
The act of naming.

intro.en: Title is a Latin stem; its items show prefixes and compounds built on the label idea.
intro.cn: title 是拉丁词干；条目展示围绕「标签」观念的前缀与复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin titulus underlies the whole family; the prefix lines below share it.
latinIntro.cn: 整个词族都建立在拉丁语 titulus 之上；下列前缀词均与之相关。

items.meaning: to give a right or a name to
items.example: The ticket entitles you to a free seat.
items.exampleCN: 这张票让你有权免费入座。

items.meaning: an official right to a benefit
items.example: Holiday pay is an entitlement.
items.exampleCN: 带薪休假是应得的权利。

items.meaning: a secondary title or film dialogue translation
items.example: We watched the film with subtitles.
items.exampleCN: 我们开着字幕看了那部电影。

items.meaning: the document proving ownership of land
items.example: The title deed is in the safe.

items.meaning: the page showing a book's full name
items.example: The title page carries the printer's mark.

items.meaning: holding a title without the full duties
items.example: He is the titular head of the firm.

items.meaning: the official name of a position
items.example: Her job title is Senior Analyst.
items.exampleCN: 她的职位是资深分析师。

items.meaning: the current champion or owner of a title
items.meaningCN: 冠军保持者；头衔持有人
items.example: The titleholder defended her crown.

definition_zh: 到；向；对；用于不定式；直到
definition_en: in the direction of, reaching a state or limit, or marking an infinitive verb
core_image: 一支箭朝目标飞去的方向；到达某点为止的界限
scene: 信封写好了地址，寄往北方。She mailed the letter to her cousin.
sceneCN: 这里 to 是「向、寄给」（第 1 个义项：方向或对象）；句意：她把信寄给了表姐。

derivatives.zh: to 加 -ward，义为「朝向」
to + night 复合，义为「今晚」
to + day 复合，义为「今天」

senses.title: In the direction of
senses.definition: in the direction of a place, person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 朝向某地、某人或某物
senses.example: We walked to the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们步行去车站。
senses.why: The core image is an arrow flying toward its mark.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一支朝目标飞去的箭。

senses.title: Reaching a state or limit
senses.definition: as far as a point, degree or condition
senses.definitionCN: 到达某点、某度或某种状态
senses.example: The water rose to the window sill.
senses.exampleCN: 水涨到了窗台。
senses.why: The arrow lands; the movement ends at a boundary.
senses.whyCN: 箭落下，运动止于界限。

senses.title: Marking an infinitive
senses.definition: used before the base form of a verb to form the infinitive
senses.definitionCN: 置于动词原形之前构成不定式
senses.example: She wants to travel.
senses.exampleCN: 她想去旅行。
senses.why: The word points ahead to the action, as an arrow points to a mark.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指向后面的动作，如箭指向靶。

senses.title: Given or addressed to
senses.definition: marking a recipient or the person affected
senses.definitionCN: 标示接受者或受影响者
senses.example: Give the report to the manager.
senses.exampleCN: 把报告交给经理。
senses.why: The arrow of transfer ends at a person.
senses.whyCN: 传递之箭落在人身上。

senses.title: A range in time or number
senses.definition: marking the end point of a period or a scale
senses.definitionCN: 标示时间段或数值范围的终点
senses.example: The shop is open from ten to six.
senses.exampleCN: 商店从十点营业到六点。
senses.why: Two arrows fix the two ends of a stretch.
senses.whyCN: 两支箭定出一段范围的两端。

senses.title: Compared or attached with
senses.definition: marking a comparison, a ratio or an attachment
senses.definitionCN: 标示比较、比例或 attached 关系
senses.example: The score was three to one.
senses.exampleCN: 比分是三比一。
senses.why: The arrow links one term to another in relation.
senses.whyCN: 箭把一个项与另一项关联起来。

senses.title: Reacting with a feeling
senses.definition: marking what a feeling or reaction is directed at
senses.definitionCN: 标示情感或反应所指向的对象
senses.example: To her relief, the train was late.
senses.exampleCN: 令她松口气的是，火车晚点了。
senses.why: Feeling flies like an arrow to its cause.
senses.whyCN: 情感如箭飞向它的来由。

senses.title: Back to the usual state
senses.definition: used after some verbs to show return to consciousness, order or position
senses.definitionCN: 置于某些动词后表示恢复知觉、秩序或位置
senses.example: The sailors pushed the door to.
senses.exampleCN: 水手们把门推严了。
senses.why: The arrow doubles back to where it started.
senses.whyCN: 箭折回出发点。

intro.en: To comes from Old English to, meaning toward or as far as, from a Germanic root of direction; its use before verbs hardened into the infinitive marker during Middle English.
intro.cn: to 出自古英语 to「朝向、直到」，源自日耳曼语表方向之根；置于动词前的用法在中古英语期凝固化，成为不定式标记。

items.en: The root marked direction toward a goal.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语词根标记朝向目标的方向。

items.en: To covered both place and time goals.
items.cn: 古英语 to 兼指地点与时间的目标。

items.en: To before verbs settled into the infinitive sign.
items.cn: 中古英语中 to 置于动词前定型为不定式记号。

items.en: Weak pronunciation tə spread in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 十六世纪弱读 tə 在日常口语中普及。

items.en: Modern usage spans direction, limit, recipient and infinitive.
items.cn: 现代用法涵盖方向、限度、对象与不定式。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alike tiny words; the second sorts direction neighbours.
note.cn: 第一组是形近的短词；第二组列出方向义的近邻。

entries.definition: also, or more than enough
the number after one
to perform an action
in the direction of, without necessarily arriving
up to a stated time or event
intended to belong to or be given to

normalIntro.en: Real links: go to school, to some extent, three to one, and want to travel.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：去上学、在某种程度上、三比一，以及想去旅行。

normal.en: To is the arrow every sentence aims.
normal.cn: to 是每个句子射出的箭。

normal.en: Go to school sends the arrow to a place.
normal.cn: go to school 把箭射向地点。

normal.en: Want to travel points the arrow at a verb.
normal.cn: want to travel 把箭指向动词。

normal.en: Three to one ties two numbers with one line.
normal.cn: three to one 用一条线连起两个数。

normal.en: Come to doubles the arrow back to yourself.
normal.cn: come to 让箭折回到你自己身上。

abstract.en: Every to is a small bridge between here and there.
abstract.cn: 每个 to 都是此处与彼处之间的小桥。

abstract.en: The smallest word carries the whole idea of direction.
abstract.cn: 最小的词承载着方向的整体观念。

abstract.en: An infinitive is a verb waiting behind an arrow.
abstract.cn: 不定式是候在一支箭后面的动词。

examples.en: She handed the keys to her brother.
examples.cn: 她把钥匙递给了弟弟。

examples.en: It is warmer today, close to twenty degrees.
examples.cn: 今天更暖和，接近二十度。

examples.en: He stayed to watch the end of the match.
examples.cn: 他留下来看完比赛的最后部分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「兔」——兔子「图」向萝卜飞奔，方向明确 → to 到；向

root: 单一词干：古英语 to「朝向、直到」，出自原始日耳曼语方向词根；不定式标记由方位义在句法中凝固而来。

sensesIntro.en: To points like an arrow: at places, persons, limits, comparisons and bare verbs.
sensesIntro.cn: to 像箭一样指：指地点、人、限度、比较，也指光杆动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow aimed at a mark, in space, time or grammar.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支瞄准目标的箭，见于空间、时间与语法。

branches.en: Direction and the boundary reached.
Persons and feelings as targets.
Ranges and relations between terms.
branches.cn: 项与项之间的范围与关系。

branches.en: The arrow before a bare verb.
The arrow folded back to the start.

intro.en: To is a bare particle; its items show compounds where the old sense of direction survives.
intro.cn: to 是裸露的小品词；条目展示存留古方向义的复合词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognates; to is native Germanic throughout.
latinIntro.cn: 无拉丁同源词；to 全程属本土日耳曼语源。

items.example: Today is the deadline.
Tonight will be cold.

items.meaning: on the day after this one
items.example: Tomorrow brings new chances.
They moved toward the exit.
He rocked the chair to and fro.
Sit next to me.

items.meaning: as far as; as much as
items.example: Up to ten people may enter.
She outdid her own record.

definition_zh: 烤面包片；祝酒；祝词；烤；祝酒
definition_en: sliced bread browned by heat, a call to drink in someone's honour, or to brown bread and to drink in honour
core_image: 从火里取出的焦黄面包；举杯时一句落在酒面的祝词
scene: 清晨厨房里飘出焦香味。She buttered a slice of hot toast.
sceneCN: 这里 toast 是「烤面包片」（第 1 个义项：烤黄的面包）；句意：她给一片热吐司抹上黄油。

derivatives.zh: toast 加 -er，义为「烤面包机；祝酒者」
toast 加 -y，义为「暖烘烘的」
toaster + oven 复合，义为「小型烤箱」

senses.title: Brown bread from heat
senses.definition: bread made crisp and brown by heating
senses.definitionCN: 经烘烤变得焦黄酥脆的面包
senses.example: Breakfast was eggs and toast.
senses.exampleCN: 早餐是鸡蛋和吐司。
senses.why: The core image is pale bread turned golden by fire.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是苍白面包被火烤成金黄。

senses.title: To brown bread by heat
senses.definition: to make bread, cheese or nuts crisp by heating them
senses.definitionCN: 把面包、奶酪或坚果烤脆
senses.example: Toast the almonds in a dry pan.
senses.exampleCN: 用干锅把杏仁烤香。
senses.why: The thing made becomes the verb that makes it.
senses.whyCN: 制成物变回制造它的动词。

senses.title: A drink in someone's honour
senses.definition: an act of raising glasses and drinking to honour a person or event
senses.definitionCN: 举杯向某人或某事致敬的饮酒行为
senses.example: They raised their glasses in a toast to the couple.
senses.exampleCN: 他们举杯向新人敬酒。
senses.why: The honoured name is dropped into the wine like spice into warmed drink.
senses.whyCN: 被致敬的名字落进酒里，如香料落入温酒。

senses.title: The words spoken at a toast
senses.definition: a short speech or sentence said while raising a glass
senses.definitionCN: 举杯时说的简短祝语
senses.example: His toast made everyone laugh.
senses.exampleCN: 他的祝词让大家都笑了。
senses.why: The act of honouring extends to the words that carry it.
senses.whyCN: 致敬之举延伸为承载它的言辞。

senses.title: To drink in honour of someone
senses.definition: to honour a person by raising glasses and drinking
senses.definitionCN: 以举杯饮酒的方式向某人致敬
senses.example: The team toasted their coach after the final.
senses.exampleCN: 决赛后全队向教练敬酒。
senses.why: The noun of the act becomes the act itself.
senses.whyCN: 行为的名词变成行为本身。

senses.title: A person honoured by many
senses.definition: a person widely celebrated, as in the toast of the town
senses.definitionCN: 广受赞誉的人，如 the toast of the town
senses.example: Overnight the young singer became the toast of the town.
senses.exampleCN: 一夜之间，年轻歌手成了全城的宠儿。
senses.why: Many glasses raised to one name make the person the drink's purpose.
senses.whyCN: 众多酒杯为同一个名字举起，此人便成了酒的意义。

senses.title: Warm as toast: warmed through
senses.definition: informal for comfortably warm, as near a fire
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指暖和舒适，如在火边
senses.example: By the stove we were as warm as toast.
senses.exampleCN: 在炉边我们暖烘烘的。
senses.why: The fire that browns bread also warms people.
senses.whyCN: 烤黄面包的火同样温暖人。

senses.title: Toasted: condemned or finished
senses.definition: informal for someone or something doomed, or harshly criticized
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指注定失败或遭严厉批评
senses.example: Without the data, the project is toast.
senses.exampleCN: 没有数据，项目就完蛋了。
senses.why: What the fire takes is gone; the burnt state became slang for ruin.
senses.whyCN: 被火夺走的便不复存在；焦糊态成了完蛋的俚语。

intro.en: Toast comes from Old French toster, to roast, from Latin tostare, a frequentative of torrere, to parch. The drinking sense grew from spiced bread dropped into warm wine at feasts.
intro.cn: toast 出自古法语 toster「烘烤」，源自拉丁语 torrere 的反复动词 tostare「烤干」。饮酒义源于宴会上把香料面包投入温酒的做法。

items.en: Torrere meant to parch and dry with heat.
items.cn: 拉丁语 torrere 意为用热力烤干。

items.en: Toster kept the sense of roasting before a fire.
items.cn: 古法语 toster 保留在火前烘烤之义。

items.en: Toast named the browned slice of bread.
items.cn: 中古英语 toast 指烤黄的面包片。

items.en: Spiced toast was floated in warm wine at banquets.
items.cn: 十五世纪宴会上把香料吐司浸入温酒。

items.en: A celebrated lady was likened to the flavouring toast, giving the drinking sense.
items.cn: 十七世纪把受赞美的女士比作酒中的调味吐司，产生敬酒义。

items.en: Modern usage keeps bread, fire, honour and slang for ruin.
items.cn: 现代用法兼有面包、火、致敬与完蛋的俚语。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alike -oast words; the second sorts honour-and-heat neighbours.
note.cn: 第一组是 -oast 形近词；第二组列出致敬与受热义的近邻。

entries.definition: to cook with dry heat, especially meat
the land beside the sea
entries.definitionCN: 海岸；拼写相近而非同词

entries.definition: to talk with too much pride
a friendly word said while raising glasses
to cook bread or cakes in an oven
to greet or honour someone formally

normalIntro.en: Real links: hot toast, propose a toast, warm as toast, and the project is toast.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：热吐司、提议举杯、暖烘烘，以及项目完蛋了。

normal.en: Toast is bread turned golden by fire.
normal.cn: toast 是被火烤成金黄的面包。

normal.en: A toast drops a name into the wine.
normal.cn: 敬酒是把一个名字落进酒里。

normal.en: Warm as toast borrows the heat of the hearth.
normal.cn: warm as toast 借用了炉火的热。

normal.en: The singer became the toast of the town.
normal.cn: 歌手成了全城举杯致敬的人。

normal.en: If the project is toast, the fire has won.
normal.cn: 若项目完蛋，那就是火赢了。

abstract.en: Every toast is heat marking a change of state.
abstract.cn: 每个 toast 都是热力标记的状态改变。

abstract.en: Honour, like spice, is dropped into the cup.
abstract.cn: 敬意如香料，被投进杯中。

abstract.en: What fire finishes, language calls toast.
abstract.cn: 被火终结之物，语言称之为 toast。

examples.en: She dropped two slices of bread into the toaster.
examples.cn: 她把两片面包放进烤面包机。

examples.en: The captain gave a toast to the crew.
examples.cn: 船长向全体船员敬酒。

examples.en: Toast the nuts until they smell sweet.
examples.cn: 把坚果烤到散发出香味。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吐司」——toast 的音译本尊，烤黄的面包片 → toast 吐司；祝酒

root: 单一词干：拉丁语 torrere「烤干」的反复式 tostare，经古法语 toster 进入英语。核心意象是热力使物焦黄；饮酒义由浸酒的香料吐司引申。

sensesIntro.en: Toast browns bread, warms rooms, and raises honoured names in wine.
sensesIntro.cn: toast 烤黄面包、温暖房间，也把受敬的名字举进酒杯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fire turning pale things golden, and names dropped into raised glasses.
core.cn: 核心意象：火把苍白之物烤成金黄，名字落入举起的酒杯。

branches.en: Bread, browning and borrowed warmth.
branches.cn: 面包、烤制与借来的温暖。

branches.en: Raising glasses, words and the act itself.
The person everyone drinks to.
Slang: finished by the fire.
The wine custom that links bread and honour.
branches.cn: 连接面包与敬意的酒俗。

intro.en: Toast is a Latin stem through French; its items show agent nouns and warm compounds.
intro.cn: toast 是经法语传入的拉丁词干；条目展示施动名词与温暖的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin torrere also gives torrid, scorch and roast family words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 torrere 还派生 torrid（炎热的）与 roast 一族。

items.meaning: a machine for browning bread; one who proposes toasts
items.example: The toaster popped up two slices.
items.exampleCN: 烤面包机弹出两片吐司。

items.example: The room felt toasty by evening.

items.meaning: bread dipped in egg and fried
items.example: We had French toast and syrup.
items.exampleCN: 我们吃了法式吐司配糖浆。

items.example: Melt the cheese in the toaster oven.

items.meaning: to cook with dry heat; meat so cooked
items.example: They roast a chicken every Sunday.
The torrid summer dried the fields.
The iron scorched the shirt.

items.meaning: the official who proposes toasts at formal dinners
items.example: The toastmaster opened the banquet.

definition_zh: 今天；现今；当今时代
definition_en: on this day, at the present time, or the present age
core_image: 日历上被圈住的当前一页
scene: 闹钟一响，新的一页翻开。Today she decided to start running.
sceneCN: 这里 today 是「今天」（第 1 个义项：当前这一天）；句意：今天她决定开始跑步。

derivatives.zh: to + night 复合，义为「今晚」
to + morrow 复合，义为「明天」
罕用复数，义为「各个今天；眼前的日子」

senses.title: On this day
senses.definition: during or on the present day
senses.definitionCN: 在当前这一天里
senses.example: The shops close early today.
senses.exampleCN: 今天商店早打烊。
senses.why: The core image is the calendar page now open.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是日历上正翻开的一页。

senses.title: The present day as a noun
senses.definition: the present day treated as a thing named
senses.definitionCN: 作为名词的当前一天
senses.example: Today is the last day of the sale.
senses.exampleCN: 今天是促销最后一天。
senses.why: The open page becomes a named object.
senses.whyCN: 翻开的一页变成被指名的对象。

senses.title: At the present time
senses.definition: at the current period, as opposed to the past
senses.definitionCN: 在当前时期，与过去相对
senses.example: Today, people work from home more often.
senses.exampleCN: 如今人们更常在家办公。
senses.why: The single day widens into the whole present stretch.
senses.whyCN: 单独的一天拓宽为整个当下时段。

senses.title: The present age
senses.definition: the present era considered as a period of history
senses.definitionCN: 被视为历史时期的当今时代
senses.example: The young of today grew up with phones.
senses.exampleCN: 当代年轻人是伴随手机长大的。
senses.why: The present stretch becomes an age with its own character.
senses.whyCN: 当下时段变成有自身特征的时代。

senses.title: Today's: belonging to this day
senses.definition: used in the possessive to attach something to the present day
senses.definitionCN: 用所属格把某物系于今天
senses.example: Today's meeting has been moved to Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 今天的会议改到周五。
senses.why: The day owns what happens inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这一天拥有发生在其中的一切。

senses.title: As of today: from this date
senses.definition: starting from the present day
senses.definitionCN: 从今天开始
senses.example: As of today, the new rules apply.
senses.exampleCN: 自今日起新规生效。
senses.why: The page is fixed as a starting point.
senses.whyCN: 这一页被定为起点。

senses.title: From today on: the continuing present
senses.definition: used with on to mark a change that holds from now forward
senses.definitionCN: 与 on 连用，标记自当下延续的改变
senses.example: From today on, no phones at the table.
senses.exampleCN: 从今天起，餐桌上不许用手机。
senses.why: The page stays open into the days after it.
senses.whyCN: 这一页向着之后的日子持续敞开。

senses.title: Up to today: the reached present
senses.definition: used with until or so far to mark the present as an end point
senses.definitionCN: 与 until、so far 连用，把当下作为终点
senses.example: Until today, nobody had noticed the error.
senses.exampleCN: 直到今天才有人注意到这个错误。
senses.why: The arrow of time lands on the open page.
senses.whyCN: 时间之箭落在翻开的一页上。

intro.en: Today is a native compound of to, in the old sense of at or on, plus day, first recorded in Old English as to dæg, on this day.
intro.cn: today 是本土复合词：to 取古义「在、于」，加 day，古英语已见 to dæg「在今天」。

items.en: To dæg meant on this day, the phrase already fixed.
items.cn: 古英语 to dæg 意为在今天，短语已固定。

items.en: To day merged into one word, today.
items.cn: 中古英语 to day 合写为 today。

items.en: The noun use, as in today is the day, spread.
items.cn: 十六世纪名词用法普及。

items.en: The present-age sense grew with newspapers and modern talk.
items.cn: 十九世纪随报刊语言长出当代义。

items.en: Today now names the day, the time and the age.
items.cn: 现代 today 兼指今天、如今与当代。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alike time words; the second sorts present-day neighbours.
note.cn: 第一组是形近的时间词；第二组列出当今义的近邻。

entries.definition: the two-word older form, now written as one
entries.definitionCN: 旧式分写，今已合为一词

entries.definition: the same compound built on night
entries.definitionCN: 以 night 构成的同型复合词

entries.definition: a warm sweet drink; spelled close but a different word
entries.definitionCN: 热甜酒；拼写相近而非同词

entries.definition: at this very moment
at the present period of time
the current period of history

normalIntro.en: Real links: today's paper, as of today, the young of today, and from today on.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：今天的报纸、自今日起、当代年轻人，以及从今天起。

normal.en: Today is the calendar page now open.
normal.cn: today 是日历上正翻开的一页。

normal.en: The noun today names that page.
normal.cn: 名词 today 给这一页命名。

normal.en: Today, the page widens into the whole present.
normal.cn: 表如今的 today 把一页拓宽为整个当下。

normal.en: As of today fixes the page as a start line.
normal.cn: as of today 把这一页定为起跑线。

normal.en: From today on keeps the page open for good.
normal.cn: from today on 让这一页永远敞开。

abstract.en: Every today is the meeting place of past arrow and future hope.
abstract.cn: 每个 today 都是过去之箭与未来之盼的相遇处。

abstract.en: Only today can be acted on directly.
abstract.cn: 唯有今天可以被直接行动。

abstract.en: The present age is just many todays walking together.
abstract.cn: 当代不过是无数个今天并肩同行。

examples.en: Today is warmer than yesterday.
examples.cn: 今天比昨天暖和。

examples.en: The factory of today looks nothing like the old works.
examples.cn: 如今的工厂与旧时的工场判若云泥。

examples.en: As of today, tickets must be booked online.
examples.cn: 自今日起，购票须在网上进行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特到」——今天的机会「特」别「到」位，抓紧今天 → today 今天；如今

root: 单一词干：本土复合词 to（古义「在、于」）+ day（日），古英语 to dæg 已定型。与 tonight、tomorrow 同属 to- 家族。

sensesIntro.en: Today opens one day, then widens into the present time and the present age.
sensesIntro.cn: today 先打开一天，再拓宽为当下时段与当今时代。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the calendar page currently open, then stretched into an era.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历上正翻开的一页，随后拉伸为一个时代。

branches.en: The day itself and what belongs to it.
branches.cn: 这一天本身及其所属之物。

Today as the point time lands on.

latinIntro.cn: 无拉丁同源词；today 是完全本土的英语词。

items.example: Stay in tonight.
Tomorrow the market opens.
Write today's date on the form.

items.example: Travel is easy in today's world.

items.example: Keep the records up to date.
Nowadays almost everyone has a phone.
The sun is strong at midday.

items.meaning: the hours when it is light
items.example: Sleep in the daytime, work at night.

definition_zh: 脚趾；趾部；鞋头
definition_en: one of the five end parts of the foot, or the front part of a shoe
core_image: 脚最前端可以分出的五根小枝
scene: 光脚踩在地板上，冰凉。He tested the water with his toe.
sceneCN: 这里 toe 是「脚趾」（第 1 个义项：脚的前端部分）；句意：他用脚趾试探水温。

derivatives.zh: tip + toe 复合，义为「脚尖；踮脚走」
toe 加 -less，义为「无趾的；露趾的」
toe + cap 复合，义为「鞋头加固片」

senses.title: One of the five ends of the foot
senses.definition: one of the five separate parts at the front of the foot
senses.definitionCN: 脚前端的五个分部之一
senses.example: A stone bruised his little toe.
senses.exampleCN: 一块石头硌伤了他的小脚趾。
senses.why: The core image is the foot's front branching into fingers.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是脚的前端分出五根小枝。

senses.title: The front part of the foot
senses.definition: the whole front part of the foot, as in touching with the toes
senses.definitionCN: 脚的整个前部，如以足尖触碰
senses.example: She reached the line with her toes.
senses.exampleCN: 她的足尖够到了线。
senses.why: The five parts act together as one front edge.
senses.whyCN: 五根脚趾并作一条前缘。

senses.title: The front of a shoe or sock
senses.definition: the part of a shoe or sock that covers the toes
senses.definitionCN: 鞋袜罩住脚趾的部分
senses.example: The shoes have steel toe caps.
senses.exampleCN: 这鞋有钢制鞋头。
senses.why: The covering takes the name of the part it covers.
senses.whyCN: 覆盖物以所覆盖部位命名。

senses.title: To touch or kick with the toe
senses.definition: to hit, kick or touch something with the toe of the foot or shoe
senses.definitionCN: 以脚尖或鞋尖触碰、踢击
senses.example: He just toed the ball forward.
senses.exampleCN: 他只用脚尖把球往前一捅。
senses.why: The part becomes the tool and then the act.
senses.whyCN: 部位变成工具，再变成动作。

senses.title: Toe the line: obey the rules
senses.definition: to accept authority or rules, from putting a toe exactly on a mark
senses.definitionCN: 服从权威或规则，源于脚尖抵住标线
senses.example: The new staff soon learned to toe the line.
senses.exampleCN: 新员工很快学会了守规矩。
senses.why: A toe on a mark stands for exact obedience.
senses.whyCN: 脚尖抵线代表毫厘不差的服从。

senses.title: Keep on your toes: stay alert
senses.definition: to remain ready and alert for sudden change
senses.definitionCN: 随时准备应对突发变化
senses.example: The quiz keeps students on their toes.
senses.exampleCN: 测验让学生始终保持警觉。
senses.why: On the toes means poised, ready to spring.
senses.whyCN: 踮起脚尖意味着蓄势待发。

senses.title: Step on toes: intrude
senses.definition: to offend someone by interfering in what they control
senses.definitionCN: 因插手他人领域而冒犯对方
senses.example: Marketing stepped on the design team's toes.
senses.exampleCN: 市场部越了设计组的界。
senses.why: Feet in a small space jostle for room.
senses.whyCN: 狭小空间里脚与脚相挤。

senses.title: Dip a toe into: try cautiously
senses.definition: to try something new in a small, careful way
senses.definitionCN: 以小而谨慎的方式尝试新事物
senses.example: She dipped a toe into online selling.
senses.exampleCN: 她试着在网上小规模卖货。
senses.why: One toe tests the temperature before the body follows.
senses.whyCN: 一根脚趾先试水温，身体随后跟进。

intro.en: Toe comes from Old English ta, a toe, from a Germanic root shared with words for fingers; Latin digitus covered both finger and toe, and English toe kept the branching-end image.
intro.cn: toe 出自古英语 ta「脚趾」，与表指的日耳曼词根同族；拉丁语 digitus 兼指手指与脚趾，英语 toe 保留了「分出的小端」意象。

items.en: The root named the branching ends of feet and hands.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语词根指手脚分出的小端。

items.en: Ta meant a toe; tā was a toe or claw.
items.cn: 古英语 ta 指脚趾。

items.en: Toe covered foot toes and shoe fronts.
items.cn: 中古英语 toe 兼指脚趾与鞋头。

items.en: Toe the line arose from military dressings on a mark.
items.cn: 十六世纪 toe the line 源于队列以脚尖抵线。

items.en: Modern idiom keeps alertness, obedience and caution in toe phrases.
items.cn: 现代习语在 toe 短语中保留警觉、服从与谨慎。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alike short words; the second sorts body-end neighbours.
note.cn: 第一组是形近短词；第二组列出身体末端义的近邻。

entries.definition: to fasten with string; spelled close but a different word
entries.definitionCN: 系；捆；拼写相近而非同词

entries.definition: the hard plate on a toe
a roof or floor block; spelled close but a different word
entries.definitionCN: 瓦片；瓷砖；拼写相近而非同词

entries.definition: one of the five end parts of the hand
the whole body part the toes belong to
the back part of the foot

normalIntro.en: Real links: the big toe, toe the line, keep on your toes, and dip a toe into.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：大脚趾、服从规矩、保持警觉，以及试水。

normal.en: A toe is one small branch of the foot's front.
normal.cn: 脚趾是脚前端的一根小枝。

normal.en: Toe the line puts one toe exactly on the mark.
normal.cn: toe the line 让脚尖毫厘不差地抵线。

normal.en: On your toes means poised like a runner.
normal.cn: on your toes 像起跑者一样蓄势。

normal.en: Stepping on toes jostles in a small space.
normal.cn: step on toes 是在狭小处相挤。

normal.en: A dipped toe tests the water for the whole body.
normal.cn: 试水的脚趾替全身探温。

abstract.en: Every toe is the edge where the body meets the world first.
abstract.cn: 每个脚趾都是身体最先触到世界的边缘。

abstract.en: Small parts carry the idioms of caution and obedience.
abstract.cn: 小小的部位承载着谨慎与服从的习语。

abstract.en: The foot has fingers too; they are called toes.
abstract.cn: 脚也有手指，它们叫 toe。

examples.en: She wiggled her toes in the sand.
examples.cn: 她在沙子里活动脚趾。

examples.en: The steel toe cap saved his foot from the falling box.
examples.cn: 钢头鞋护住了他被落箱砸到的脚。

examples.en: Reporters kept the minister on his toes all week.
examples.cn: 记者们整周都让部长不敢松懈。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「投」——脚趾一「投」，轻轻捅球入门 → toe 脚趾；用脚尖触

root: 单一词干：古英语 ta「脚趾」，出自原始日耳曼语表「分出的小端」的词根，与拉丁 digitus（指、趾）观念平行。

sensesIntro.en: Toe starts as a branching end of the foot and grows into shoes, kicks and idioms of alertness and obedience.
sensesIntro.cn: toe 始于脚上分出的小枝，长成鞋头、脚尖踢触，以及警觉与服从的习语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the front edge of the foot, split into five small ends.
core.cn: 核心意象：脚的前缘，分作五个小端。

branches.en: The toe itself and the whole front edge.
Shoe fronts and toe as a tool.
branches.cn: 鞋头与作为工具的脚尖。

branches.en: Obedience and alertness idioms.
Jostling for space.
Testing before entering.

intro.en: Toe is a short native stem; its items show compounds of shoes, feet and motion.
intro.cn: toe 是简短的本土词干；条目展示鞋、足与动作的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin digitus covers both finger and toe; English uses toe and finger separately.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 digitus 兼指指与趾；英语以 toe 与 finger 分开。

items.meaning: the end of the toe; to walk quietly on it
items.example: She tiptoed past the door.

items.meaning: the reinforcing cover over a shoe's front
items.example: Steel toecaps are standard in factories.
items.exampleCN: 工厂标准配置是钢头鞋。

items.meaning: the hard plate on a toe
items.example: He cut his toenails too short.

items.meaning: without a covered toe; without toes
items.example: Toeless sandals suit the beach.
The big toe helps you balance.
items.exampleCN: 大脚趾帮助你保持平衡。

items.example: Open-toed shoes are not allowed in the lab.
Everyone must toe the line here.

items.meaning: using heel and toe together, as in driving or walking briskly
items.example: He drove with heel-and-toe shifts.

definition_zh: 一起；共同；同时；合起来
definition_en: with each other, in company, combined into one, or at the same time
core_image: 几只手把散落的东西拢作一堆
scene: 散落的拼图在桌上一块块合拢。The children fitted the puzzle together.
sceneCN: 这里 together 是「合起来」（第 3 个义项：拼合成一体）；句意：孩子们把拼图拼好了。

derivatives.zh: together 加 -ness，义为「团结感；亲密感」
gather 加 -ing，义为「聚集；集会」
together 的词源核心，义为「收集；聚拢」

senses.title: With each other
senses.definition: in the same place or doing the same thing with others
senses.definitionCN: 与别人同在一处或做同一件事
senses.example: The family eats dinner together.
senses.exampleCN: 一家人一起吃晚饭。
senses.why: The core image is hands gathering things into one place.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是把东西拢到一处的手。

senses.title: Joined into one
senses.definition: combined or assembled so as to form a single whole
senses.definitionCN: 合拢或组装为一个整体
senses.example: Stick the two halves together.
senses.exampleCN: 把两半粘在一起。
senses.why: Gathered things touch and hold as one.
senses.whyCN: 被拢起之物相互接触，合为一体。

senses.title: Assembled or repaired
senses.definition: put into an ordered whole, as in put yourself together
senses.definitionCN: 被整理成有序整体，如 put yourself together
senses.example: She pulled herself together before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试前她稳住了情绪。
senses.why: Scattered parts are gathered back into shape.
senses.whyCN: 散乱的部分被拢回成形。

senses.title: At the same time
senses.definition: happening or done at the same moment, considered jointly
senses.definitionCN: 同一时刻发生，合并考虑
senses.example: Add the flour and sugar together.
senses.exampleCN: 把面粉和糖一起加进去。
senses.why: Two gatherings land in the same instant.
senses.whyCN: 两次聚拢落在同一瞬间。

senses.title: Successively adding up
senses.definition: considered in combination or total, as in ten years together
senses.definitionCN: 合并计算或总计，如十年加起来
senses.example: They have worked here, together, for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在此合计工作已有十年。
senses.why: Gathered amounts make a sum.
senses.whyCN: 被拢起的量构成总和。

senses.title: In agreement or union
senses.definition: in harmony or acting as one group
senses.definitionCN: 协调一致或作为一个整体行动
senses.example: The team pulled together in the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 危机中全队齐心协力。
senses.why: Gathering extends to wills and efforts.
senses.whyCN: 聚拢延伸到意志与努力。

senses.title: Together with: along with
senses.definition: used to say someone or something is included
senses.definitionCN: 表示某人或某物被包括在内
senses.example: The report, together with the charts, is ready.
senses.exampleCN: 报告连同图表都备好了。
senses.why: One gathering pulls in another beside it.
senses.whyCN: 一次聚拢把旁边另一份也带了进来。

senses.title: Self-possessed, organised
senses.definition: informal for calm, confident and well organised
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指冷静、自信、条理分明
senses.example: He came across as very together in the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 会上他显得非常沉稳。
senses.why: A person in one piece is a person gathered.
senses.whyCN: 完整如一的人，就是一个被拢好的人。

intro.en: Together is an English compound of to, in the old sense of into one group, plus gather, to collect. It has always meant brought into one.
intro.cn: together 是英语本土复合词：to 取古义「聚为一组」，加 gather「收集」。其义始终是「被拢为一」。

items.en: Togædere meant in company, into one company.
items.cn: 古英语 togædere 意为共同、聚为一伙。

items.en: Together covered both company and assembly of things.
items.cn: 中古英语 together 兼指结伴与物之聚合。

items.en: Put together grew for assembling and reckoning.
items.cn: 十六世纪 put together 用于组装与合计。

items.en: Togetherness of feeling entered the language late.
items.cn: 十九世纪后情感意义的 togetherness 进入语言。

items.en: Modern usage spans company, assembly, simultaneity and composure.
items.cn: 现代用法涵盖结伴、拼合、同时与沉稳。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alike compounds; the second sorts union neighbours.
note.cn: 第一组是形近复合词；第二组列出联合义的近邻。

entries.definition: completely, or on the whole
to collect or bring together
not a word; often confused in spelling exercises
done by two or more parties together
as a whole group
in complete agreement or unity

normalIntro.en: Real links: work together, put together, pull together, and together with.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：协作、拼合、齐心协力，以及连同。

normal.en: Together is to gather into one place.
normal.cn: together 就是 gather 到一处。

normal.en: Two halves stuck together become one thing.
normal.cn: 两半粘在一起便成一体。

normal.en: Pull yourself together: gather your scattered self.
normal.cn: pull yourself together：把散落的自己拢回来。

normal.en: Added together, separate years make a sum.
normal.cn: 加在一起，分开的年数成为总和。

normal.en: A together person is one assembled piece.
normal.cn: together 的人本身就是拼合完好的整体。

abstract.en: Every together is a small victory over scattering.
abstract.cn: 每个 together 都是对离散的一次小小胜利。

abstract.en: Hands, minds and moments can all be gathered.
abstract.cn: 手、心智与时刻皆可被拢起。

abstract.en: Unity is not sameness; it is things holding in one hand.
abstract.cn: 团结不是相同，而是诸物同握于一手。

examples.en: They walked to school together every morning.
examples.cn: 他们每天早上一起走去上学。

examples.en: Put the ingredients together in one bowl.
examples.cn: 把所有原料放进同一个碗里。

examples.en: The staff, together with the volunteers, cleaned the park.
examples.cn: 员工连同志愿者一起清理了公园。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特盖得」——特盖得住，把散的都盖拢在一起 → together 一起；合起来

root: 单一词干：本土复合词 to（古义「入于一组」）+ gather「收集」。核心始终是「拢为一」。与 gather、gathering 同族。

sensesIntro.en: Together gathers persons, parts, moments, sums and even a scattered self.
sensesIntro.cn: together 拢起人、部件、时刻、总数，甚至散乱的自己。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: scattered things drawn into one holding place.
core.cn: 核心意象：把散落之物拢进同一个地方。

branches.en: Company and acting as one.
Assembling parts, selves and order.
Moments and amounts combined.
One gathering pulling in another.
The person gathered into composure.

intro.en: Together is a fixed compound; its items show the gather family and set phrases.
intro.cn: together 是固定复合词；条目展示 gather 词族与固定短语。

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognates; together is fully native English.
latinIntro.cn: 无拉丁同源词；together 是完全本土的英语词。

items.meaning: a feeling of closeness and unity
items.example: The camp builds togetherness.
The plan is altogether different.
We had a small get-together at home.
She put the shelf together herself.
We must pull together on this.
Gather the leaves into a pile.

items.meaning: to put heads close in quiet talk or joint effort
items.example: The two teams put their heads together.

items.meaning: united for all time, in songs and vows
items.example: They promised to stay together forever.

definition_zh: 马桶；厕所；盥洗；梳妆
definition_en: a bowl used for getting rid of body waste, the room containing it, or the act of washing and dressing
core_image: 一间把污物冲走、让人收拾干净的小房间
scene: 洗手间的水声停了，门开了。The sign pointed to the toilets downstairs.
sceneCN: 这里 toilet 是「厕所」（第 2 个义项：设有马桶的房间）；句意：指示牌指向楼下的洗手间。

derivatives.zh: toilet 加 -ries，义为「梳洗化妆用品」
toilet 加 -ry，义为「一件梳洗用品」
toilet 的法语形式，义为「梳妆；装扮」

senses.title: The bowl and its fittings
senses.definition: a fixed bowl with a seat and flush, used for getting rid of body waste
senses.definitionCN: 带座圈与冲水装置的固定洁具，用于排走身体废物
senses.example: The toilet will not flush properly.
senses.exampleCN: 马桶冲水不畅。
senses.why: The core image is a small room that washes waste away.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是把污物冲走的小房间。

senses.title: The room containing the bowl
senses.definition: a room with a toilet and often a washbasin
senses.definitionCN: 设有马桶（常含洗手池）的房间
senses.example: Where are the toilets in this station?
senses.exampleCN: 这个车站的厕所在哪儿？
senses.why: The fixture names the room that holds it.
senses.whyCN: 洁具命名了容纳它的房间。

senses.title: The act of washing and dressing
senses.definition: the process of washing, grooming and dressing, especially one's toilet
senses.definitionCN: 洗漱、打理与穿衣的过程，尤指 one's toilet
senses.example: She spent an hour at her toilet before the ball.
senses.exampleCN: 舞会前她花了一个小时梳妆。
senses.why: The older sense: a cloth for grooming became the grooming itself.
senses.whyCN: 旧义：一块梳妆布演变为梳妆本身。

senses.title: Grooming articles
senses.definition: articles used in washing and grooming, as in toiletries
senses.definitionCN: 用于洗漱打理的物品，如 toiletries
senses.example: Pack your toiletries in the small bag.
senses.exampleCN: 把梳洗用品装进小包。
senses.why: The grooming act extends to its tools.
senses.whyCN: 梳妆行为延伸到它的工具。

senses.title: A cleansing or rinse of a wound
senses.definition: in medical use, the cleansing of a wound or body part
senses.definitionCN: 医学用语，指对伤口或身体部位的清洁处理
senses.example: The nurse carried out the toilet of the wound.
senses.exampleCN: 护士为伤口做了清洁处理。
senses.why: Grooming turns inward, cleaning what is hurt.
senses.whyCN: 梳妆转向内部，清洁受伤之处。

senses.title: A showy dressing cloth or costume
senses.definition: in older use, a dressing cloth, dressing table or fine costume
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法中指梳妆布、梳妆台或华服
senses.example: The duchess appeared from behind her toilet.
senses.exampleCN: 公爵夫人从梳妆台后现身。
senses.why: The cloth over the dressing table named the table, then the dress.
senses.whyCN: 梳妆台上的布命名了台子，继而是衣装。

senses.title: Canalian and regional variants of the room
senses.definition: the room sense as used across regions, from public toilets to airplane lavatories
senses.definitionCN: 房间义在各地区的用法，从公厕到机上的盥洗室
senses.example: The airplane toilets were all busy.
senses.exampleCN: 机上的洗手间全都占用了。
senses.why: The room follows its users everywhere.
senses.whyCN: 这个房间跟随使用者无处不在。

senses.title: Toilet-trained: the hygiene habit
senses.definition: compound uses about hygiene training, such as toilet-trained or toilet training
senses.definitionCN: 与卫生习惯训练相关的复合用法
senses.example: The kitten is already toilet-trained.
senses.exampleCN: 小猫已经会用猫砂了。
senses.why: The fixture becomes the standard of a habit.
senses.whyCN: 洁具成为一种习惯的标准。

intro.en: Toilet comes from French toilette, a small cloth, from toile, cloth. It named the dressing cloth, then the dressing table, the act of grooming, and finally, by polite roundabout, the fixture and the room.
intro.cn: toilet 源自法语 toilette「小布片」，出自 toile「布」。它先指梳妆布，继而梳妆台、梳妆行为，最后经雅化转指洁具与房间。

items.en: Toile meant cloth; toilette, a small cloth or dressing cover.
items.cn: 法语 toile 意为布；toilette 为小布或梳妆罩布。

items.en: Toilet named the dressing cloth and table for grooming.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语 toilet 指梳妆布与梳妆台。

items.en: One's toilet meant the act and style of dressing.
items.cn: 十七世纪 one's toilet 指梳妆的行为与样式。

items.en: Polite speech used toilet room, shortened to toilet, for the fixture.
items.cn: 十九世纪雅语以 toilet room 指盥洗间，简略为 toilet。

items.en: The fixture sense dominates; the grooming sense survives in toiletries and toilette.
items.cn: 现代以洁具义为主；梳妆义存于 toiletries 与 toilette。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alike French-flavoured words; the second sorts room neighbours.
note.cn: 第一组是带法语味的形近词；第二组列出房间义的近邻。

entries.definition: the French-styled word for one's grooming and dress
a light fabric or its printed pattern
hard exhausting work; spelled close but a different word
entries.definitionCN: 苦役；辛劳；拼写相近而非同词

entries.definition: a toilet or washroom, more formal
the American polite word for a public toilet
a room with toilets and basins

normalIntro.en: Real links: flush the toilet, toilet paper, her toilet before the ball, and toiletries.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：冲马桶、卫生纸、舞会前的梳妆，以及梳洗用品。

normal.en: A toilet begins as a small cloth on the dressing table.
normal.cn: toilet 起于梳妆台上的一小块布。

normal.en: The cloth grew into the table, the dressing, then the room.
normal.cn: 布长成台子、梳妆，再长成房间。

normal.en: Flush the toilet: the room's job is to wash away.
normal.cn: 冲马桶：这个房间的职责是冲走。

normal.en: Her toilet before the ball was an hour of grooming.
normal.cn: 舞会前的 her toilet 是一小时的梳妆。

normal.en: Toiletries are the cloth's descendants in a travel bag.
normal.cn: toiletries 是梳妆布在旅行包里的后代。

abstract.en: Every toilet is a room where cleanliness is made twice: of body and of manners.
abstract.cn: 每个 toilet 都是双重清洁之处：净身，也净礼数。

abstract.en: Euphemism walks the same road as words: from cloth to bowl.
abstract.cn: 委婉语与词语走同一条路：从一块布到一只马桶。

abstract.en: Grooming began at a small cloth and ended in porcelain.
abstract.cn: 梳妆始于一块小布，终结于瓷器。

examples.en: Please flush the toilet after use.
examples.cn: 用后请冲马桶。

examples.en: The hotel has clean public toilets on each floor.
examples.cn: 酒店每层都有干净的公共卫生间。

examples.en: A small bag of toiletries hung by the sink.
examples.cn: 洗手池边挂着一个小小的梳洗包。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「套里特」——马桶套里特别的干净，正是 toilet → toilet 马桶；厕所

root: 单一词干：法语 toile「布」→ toilette「小布、梳妆罩布」，进入英语后经「梳妆布→梳妆台→梳妆→洁具→房间」的委婉链条完成词义迁移。

sensesIntro.en: Toilet travels from a dressing cloth to grooming, then to the porcelain fixture and its room.
sensesIntro.cn: toilet 从一块梳妆布出发，走过梳妆，抵达瓷制洁具及其房间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small cloth that grows into a room for washing away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块小布长成一间用来冲走与洗净的房间。

branches.en: The grooming line: act, tools, dress.
The fixture line: bowl, room, regions.
branches.cn: 洁具线：马桶、房间、各地称呼。

branches.en: Cleansing turned medical.
The habit built around the fixture.
The room named by its fixture.

intro.en: Toilet is a French stem; its items show the cloth family and hygiene compounds.
intro.cn: toilet 是法语词干；条目展示布料词族与卫生复合词。

latinIntro.en: French toile traces to Latin tela, a woven cloth; the weaving root underlies the family.
latinIntro.cn: 法语 toile 追溯到拉丁语 tela「织物」；词族皆植根于织造。

items.example: The roll of toilet paper is empty.

items.meaning: the ring seat of a toilet
items.example: Put the toilet seat down.

items.meaning: grooming articles such as soap and shampoo
items.example: Free toiletries are provided.
She completed her toilette with a hat.
items.exampleCN: 她以一顶帽子完成装扮。

items.meaning: teaching a child to use the toilet
items.example: Toilet training takes patience.

items.meaning: a brush for cleaning the bowl
items.example: Replace the toilet brush each season.

items.meaning: a small part; to clean thoroughly (military)
items.example: They detailed the barracks floor.
items.exampleCN: 他们把营房地板彻底刷洗了。

items.meaning: a light woven fabric or its printed design
items.example: The curtains were printed toile.
items.exampleCN: 窗帘印着传统图案花布。

definition_zh: 番茄；西红柿
definition_en: a soft round red fruit eaten as a vegetable, growing on vines
core_image: 藤蔓上挂着的软红圆果，一捏就出汁
scene: 菜园里藤架上挂满红果子。She sliced a tomato for the salad.
sceneCN: 这里 tomato 是「番茄」（第 1 个义项：这种果实本身）；句意：她切了一个番茄做沙拉。

derivatives.zh: tomato 加 -ey，义为「番茄味的；番茄浓的」
beefsteak + tomato 复合，义为「牛排番茄（大果品种）」

senses.title: The red fruit eaten as food
senses.definition: a soft round juicy fruit, usually red, eaten raw or cooked
senses.definitionCN: 柔软多汁的圆果，通常红色，可生食可熟用
senses.example: The soup needs one more tomato.
senses.exampleCN: 汤里还要再加一个番茄。
senses.why: The core image is a red globe that yields juice at a squeeze.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一捏即出汁的红色圆果。

senses.title: The vine plant that bears it
senses.definition: the plant, a sprawling vine of the nightshade family, that produces tomatoes
senses.definitionCN: 结番茄的植物，茄科蔓生藤本
senses.example: Tomatoes ripen late in cool summers.
senses.exampleCN: 凉夏时节番茄成熟得晚。
senses.why: The fruit's name covers the bearer as well.
senses.whyCN: 果名兼指结它的植株。

senses.title: Tomato as processed food
senses.definition: tomatoes prepared as sauce, paste, juice or ketchup
senses.definitionCN: 加工为酱汁、膏、汁或番茄酱的番茄
senses.example: Stir in two spoons of tomato paste.
senses.exampleCN: 搅入两勺番茄膏。
senses.why: The fruit's name travels with it into every jar.
senses.whyCN: 果名随果实走进每一只罐瓶。

senses.title: Varieties by size and colour
senses.definition: named varieties such as cherry tomato, beefsteak or yellow tomato
senses.definitionCN: 樱桃番茄、牛排番茄、黄番茄等品种名
senses.example: Cherry tomatoes sweeten the plate.
senses.exampleCN: 樱桃番茄给盘子添甜。
senses.why: A common name forks into a market shelf of kinds.
senses.whyCN: 统名分叉出货架上的诸品种。

senses.title: Botanically a fruit, legally a vegetable
senses.definition: classified as a fruit in botany but treated as a vegetable in cooking and trade
senses.definitionCN: 植物学上属果实，烹饪与贸易中按蔬菜对待
senses.example: In customs law the tomato is a vegetable.
senses.exampleCN: 按关税法，番茄算蔬菜。
senses.why: Two systems hang different labels on one red globe.
senses.whyCN: 两套体系给同一颗红果挂上不同标签。

senses.title: Rotten tomato: thrown in protest
senses.definition: tomatoes as objects thrown at bad performers, giving the idiom rotten tomatoes
senses.definitionCN: 番茄被投向失败的演出，衍生 rotten tomatoes 之说
senses.example: The play would have earned rotten tomatoes.
senses.exampleCN: 这出戏本会招来烂番茄。
senses.why: The soft red fruit is the cheapest and messiest protest.
senses.whyCN: 软红果是最廉价又最狼藉的抗议。

senses.title: Tomato red: the colour
senses.definition: the bright red of ripe tomatoes used as a colour name
senses.definitionCN: 以熟番茄之色命名的鲜红
senses.example: She painted the door tomato red.
senses.exampleCN: 她把门漆成番茄红。
senses.why: The ripe fruit sets a standard of red.
senses.whyCN: 熟果定下一种红色的标准。

senses.title: Love apple: the older name
senses.definition: the historical name love apple for the tomato, from a mistranslation of its early names
senses.definitionCN: 番茄的历史别名 love apple，源于早期名称的误译
senses.example: Old seed lists sold love apples.
senses.exampleCN: 旧种子名录卖的是「爱情苹果」。
senses.why: A mistaken name once travelled with the fruit across Europe.
senses.whyCN: 一个误译之名曾随果实走遍欧洲。

intro.en: Tomato comes from Spanish tomate, borrowed from Nahuatl tomatl, the Aztec name for the fruit. English altered the ending by folk association with potato.
intro.cn: tomato 经西班牙语 tomate 借自纳瓦特尔语 tomatl（阿兹特克人对该果的称呼）；英语词尾受 potato 影响而民间化改形。

items.en: Tomatl named the round green-then-red fruit in Mexico.
items.cn: 纳瓦特尔语 tomatl 指墨西哥先绿后红的圆果。

items.en: Tomate carried the fruit across the Atlantic to Europe.
items.cn: 十六世纪西班牙语 tomate 把果实带过大西洋。

items.en: Pomodoro, golden apple, marked early yellow varieties.
items.cn: 意大利语 pomodoro「金苹果」记录了早期黄色品种。

items.en: Tomato entered English, first written tomate and love apple.
items.cn: 十七世纪 tomato 进入英语，初作 tomate 与 love apple。

items.en: The spelling tomato spread by analogy with potato.
items.cn: 十八世纪仿 potato 而定形拼写 tomato。

items.en: British and American pronunciations split, both thriving.
items.cn: 英式与美式读音分化，并行不悖。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alike -ato words; the second sorts kitchen-garden neighbours.
note.cn: 第一组是 -ato 形近词；第二组列出菜园邻伴。

entries.definition: a root vegetable, grown underground
the Spanish form of the same word
a violent rotating windstorm
the plant family that includes tomato and potato
another New World fruit used as a vegetable
a thick tomato sauce for food

normalIntro.en: Real links: tomato sauce, cherry tomatoes, rotten tomatoes, and tomato red.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：番茄酱汁、樱桃番茄、烂番茄，以及番茄红。

normal.en: A tomato is a red globe that yields at a squeeze.
normal.cn: 番茄是一捏即软的红圆果。

normal.en: The name crossed an ocean from Aztec gardens.
normal.cn: 这个名字从阿兹特克菜园跨洋而来。

normal.en: Botany calls it fruit; the kitchen calls it vegetable.
normal.cn: 植物学称它为果，厨房称它为菜。

normal.en: Rotten tomatoes mark the worst shows.
normal.cn: 烂番茄标记最糟的演出。

normal.en: Tomato red is ripe enough to eat with the eyes.
normal.cn: 番茄红熟得可以用眼睛来吃。

abstract.en: Every tomato carries two names: one from Mexico, one from a mistake.
abstract.cn: 每颗番茄都带着两个名字：一个来自墨西哥，一个来自误译。

abstract.en: Categories are labels; the fruit stays red either way.
abstract.cn: 分类只是标签，果实照样红。

abstract.en: The juiciest arguments, like tomatoes, splatter when thrown.
abstract.cn: 最汁液四溅的争论，如番茄般掷地开花。

examples.en: He grew tomatoes on the balcony all summer.
examples.cn: 他整个夏天在阳台上种番茄。

examples.en: The sauce is just tomatoes, garlic and oil.
examples.cn: 这酱只用番茄、蒜和油。

examples.en: Slice the tomatoes and lay them on the bread.
examples.cn: 把番茄切片铺在面包上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特没汁」——不对，反着记：番茄「特」别「没」「汁」就坏了；多汁才是好 tomato → tomato 番茄

root: 单一词干：纳瓦特尔语 tomatl「番茄」，经西班牙语 tomate、英语 tomato。词尾 -o 受 potato 类化；与「爱情苹果」旧名并行。

sensesIntro.en: Tomato names a fruit, its vine, its jars, its varieties and even a colour.
sensesIntro.cn: tomato 既指果实，也指藤蔓、罐中之酱、货架诸品种，乃至一种颜色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soft red globe ripening on a vine, yielding juice at a squeeze.
core.cn: 核心意象：藤上熟软的红圆果，一捏出汁。

branches.en: The fruit and the plant that bears it.
Jars, sauces and shelf varieties.
Two labels on one globe.
Thrown fruit and its colour standard.
branches.cn: 被掷的果实与它的色彩标准。

branches.en: The mistaken love apple of old lists.
branches.cn: 旧名录里误译的爱情苹果。

intro.en: Tomato is a borrowed stem; its items show compounds of kitchen and market.
intro.cn: tomato 是外来词干；条目展示厨房与市场的复合词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root; tomato is Nahuatl through Spanish, unlike the Latin solanum of botany.
latinIntro.cn: tomato 无拉丁词根，源自纳瓦特尔语经西班牙语；植物学另用拉丁 solanum。

items.example: Cover the pasta with tomato sauce.
A spoon of tomato paste deepens the stew.
items.exampleCN: 一勺番茄膏让炖菜更浓。

items.example: Halve the cherry tomatoes for the salad.
items.exampleCN: 把樱桃番茄对半切开放进沙拉。

items.example: Stake each tomato plant early.
items.exampleCN: 尽早给每株番茄立支架。

items.meaning: a very large flat variety for slicing
items.example: A beefsteak tomato fills the plate.
items.exampleCN: 一个牛排番茄就能铺满盘子。

items.meaning: a tomato dried in the sun for storage
items.example: Chop the sun-dried tomatoes finely.
The stew turned rich and tomatoey.

items.meaning: the Italian word for tomato; also a timing method
items.meaningCN: 意大利语「番茄」；亦指番茄钟计时法
items.example: She studies in pomodoro intervals.
